The definite case of the petitioner is that the property of respondent No.1 bearing Survey No.13/1 (Site No.241) measuring 111.48 Square Meters of Marasuru Agrahara village, Anekal Taluk has been acquired under Preliminary Notification dated 24.01.2019 and Final Notification dated 23.01.2020.

The respondent No.3 has passed the award and awarded a total compensation amount of Rs.13,33,648/- (after deduction of TDS) in respect of 111.48 Sq. Meters, which has been received by the respondent No.1 under protest.
Subsequently, on 16.01.2023 the respondent No.1 has filed the application for enhancing the compensation at the rate of Rs.5,000/- per Square feet.

Accordingly,
the application is taken by the respondent No.2 for consideration.

Further there was absolutely no whisper about the alleged sale deed referred by the respondent No.2 in the impugned Arbitral Award and at the same time, no such sale deed was produced in the arbitral proceedings to indicate that the market value of NA lands acquired in Marasuru Agrahara village was Rs. 26,910/-

Point: Before proceeding further in this case, it is relevant to note admitted and undisputed facts in this case.

The respondent No.1 Sri.
Sujith Vijayraghavan is an owner of the property bearing Sy. No.13/1 (Site No.241)
measuring to an extent of 111.48 Square Meters of Marasuru village and the said property has been acquired for widening of NH-844 under Preliminary Notification dated 24.01.2019 and Final Notification dated 23.01.2020, is an admitted fact.
It is also admitted and undisputed fact that a sum of Rs.13,33,648/- was disbursed to the respondent No. 1 as compensation in respect of 111.48 Square Meters.

.10. Subsequent to the receipt of compensation or passing of the award, the respondent No. 1 Sri. Sujith Vijayraghavan filed an application on 16.01.2023 before the respondent No.2 claiming that he is entitled for compensation at the rate of Rs.5,000/- per Square feet.
On basis of the said application, the respondent No. 2 held an inquiry and passed order in LAQ / ARB / NH- A.P. No.10/2025 844 / CR / 242/ 2022-23 dated 03.10.2024.

The respondent No.2 in its order redetermined the market value as on the date of Preliminary Notification which is Rs.26,910/- per Square Meters and since Rs.4,200/- per Square Meters has already been awarded, the same is deducted from Rs.26,910/- per Square Meters and 25% of Rs.22,710/-
i.e., the remaining amount is taken as the market value which comes to Rs. 5,678/- per Square Meters.

.11. In the case on hand, the LAO/ respondent No.3 passed the award under New Act i.e., Right to Fair Compensation and Transparency in Land Acquisition, Rehabilitation and Resettlement Act,

sentences.text: In view of the aforesaid definite contention, it is just and necessary to see what are the criteria to determine the market value of the acquired land as per new Act has to be considered by this Court.

Section 26 of Right to Fair Compensation and Transparency in Land Acquisition, Rehabilitation and Resettlement Act, 2013 speaks about determination of market value of the land by the Collector,
Section 27 of Right to Fair Compensation and Transparency in Land Acquisition, Rehabilitation and Resettlement Act, 2013 speaks about A.P. No.10/2025 determination of amount of compensation,
Section 28 of Right to Fair Compensation and Transparency in Land Acquisition, Rehabilitation and Resettlement Act, 2013 speaks about parameter considered by the Collector in determination of the award and Section 29 of Right to Fair Compensation and Transparency in Land Acquisition,
Rehabilitation and Resettlement Act, 2013 speaks about determination of value of the things attached to the land or building. Section 30 of Land Acquisition Act speaks about award of solatium.

In the context of this case, it is just and relevant to note Sections 26 and 28 of the Right to Fair Compensation and Transparency in Land Acquisition, Rehabilitation and Resettlement Act, 2013,
that reads as under:
"26. Determination of market value of land by Collector- (1) The Collector shall adopt the following criteria in assessing and determining the market value of the land,
namely:--
(a) the minimum land value, if any, specified in the Indian Stamp Act, 1899 for the registration of sale deeds or agreements to sell, as the case may be, in the area, where the land is situated;
or A.P. No.10/2025 (b) the average sale price for similar type of land situated in the nearest village or nearest vicinity area; or (c) consented amount of compensation as agreed upon under sub-section (2) of section 2 in case of acquisition of lands for private companies or for public private partnership projects, whichever is higher:

sentences.text: The first schedule to the Act is in accordance with Section 30(2) of the New Act which shows that the Collector shall issue individual awards detailing the particulars of compensation payable and the details of payment of the compensation as specified in the first schedule.

In the aforesaid facts whenever there is an application for enhancement of compensation before the Arbitrator is filed then it is the duty of the Arbitrator to see that whether the LAO followed Sections 26 to 30 of A.P. No.10/2025 the New Act along with first schedule to the Act.
If at all the award has been passed in-consonance with the aforesaid provisions of law/new Act, certainly the Arbitrator cannot intervene with the award passed by the LAO.

Therefore, in the case on hand, it is for the petitioner to prove that the award passed by the LAO / respondent No.3 is in-consonance with the aforesaid provisions of law and the respondent No.1 has to prove that the award passed by the LAO / respondent No.3 is not in consonance with the aforesaid provision of law.
As such, he has filed the petition before the Arbitrator / respondent No.2 and the respondent No.2 by considering all those facts enhanced the compensation.

.13. The definite grievance of the petitioner in this case is that the Arbitrator has enhanced the compensation on the basis of the sale deed that was not at all the part of the arbitration proceedings.

The Arbitrator in the judgment at the last paragraph at page observed that the basis for the enhancement is the sale A.P. No.10/2025 deed produced in a case of L.Venugopal and B.Prabhakar Reddy in case bearing No.LAQ/ARB/NH- 844/CR/88.99/2021-22 but the said sale deed was not at all placed before the respondent No.2 and the date of execution of said sale deed is also not made known to the parties to the proceedings.

This court is unable to understand whether the said sale deed was executed at the time of preliminary notification or the said sale deed was subsequent to the National Highways Authority Of India vs Sujith Vijayraghavan on 3 February, 2026 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/123075162/
6 preliminary notification.

sentences.text: The respondent No.1 is also not filed the said document.

The petitioner further claims that the petitioner is totally unaware of the said sale deed and the Arbitrator enhanced the compensation on the basis of the said sale deed without that has been relied and produced by the 1st respondent.
.14. I have closely perused the award passed by the Arbitrator / respondent No.2.

The Arbitrator till the 2nd paragraph at page No. 5 of her judgment not stated any reason for her award but only stated about the respective contentions of the parties as well as A.P. No.10/2025 acquisition of property by issuing notifications.

In the last paragraph of the judgment/award, it is observed by the Arbitrator /
respondent No.2 that Arbitrator is awarding or enhancing the compensation on the basis of the sale deed produced in the case of L. Venugopal and B. Prabhakar Reddy that has been said to be produced in LAQ/ARB/NH-844/CR/88,99/2021-22.
Except the said reasons, nothing has been stated or given any reasons for enhancement.
Therefore it is clear that the respondent No.1 not claimed the enhancement of the compensation on the basis of the sale deed referred by the Arbitrator in the judgment.

.15. Further the Arbitrator in the order assigned reason for enhancement of compensation that the enhancement is in accordance with enhancement made in a case of Sri. L. Venugopal and Sri. B.
Prabhakar Reddy in LAQ / ARB / NH-844 / CR / 88,99 / 2021-22.

Even the said award is not found in the trial Court records and there is no material on record to show that the respondent No.1 insisted the Arbitrator to award the A.P. No.10/2025 amount of compensation equivalent to the award of compensation awarded in the said case of Sri. L. Venugopal and Sri. B. Prabhakar Reddy.

.16. The petitioner also claimed that whatever the document relied by the respondent No. 2 for enhancing the compensation is not brought to the notice of the petitioner before passing the award/judgment.
The award also discloses that the photographs produced by the petitioner to show development of properties but such photographs are not found in the trial Court records.
Accordingly, claimed that such award is liable to be set aside as per Section 24 of National Highways Authority Act.
In this context, the petitioner relied on the decision reported in (2019) 15 SCC 131 in a case of Ssangyong Engineering and Construction Company Limited Vs. National Highways Authority of India.

entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: It is true that in the said decision, the Hon'ble Supreme Court held that whatever the document relied by the Arbitrator shall be brought to the notice of the parties, so that the parties can make submission or give a A.P. No.10/2025 rebuttal evidence about such documents.

However,
in the case on hand, such sale deed and the award passed in the case of Sri. L. Venugopal and Sri. B.
Prabhakar Reddy as well as photographs are not found in the record received from the Arbitrator.

.17. The claim of the petitioner is that the respondent No.3 passed the award in accordance with Sections 26 to 30 as well as first schedule of the Right to Fair Compensation and Transparency in Land Acquisition, Rehabilitation and Resettlement Act, 2013.

sentences.text: In this context, the petitioner produced guidance value of the acquired land which is published in Gazette notification dated 24.01.2019.

As per the said document, the market value determined for the properties at Marasuru village is at Rs.26,910/- per Square Meter along with determination of market value for all types of land and building etc.

Section 26(1)(a) states that the market value, if any, specified in the Indian Stamp Act, 1899 (2 of 1899) for the registration of sale deeds or agreements to sell, as the case may National Highways Authority Of India vs Sujith Vijayraghavan on 3 February, 2026 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/123075162/
7 be, A.P. No.10/2025 in the area, where the land is situated is to be considered to determine the market value of the acquired property.

sentences.text: Therefore, as per the said provision, the Arbitrator has to determine the market value of the acquired land on the basis of the market value specified in the Indian Stamp Act.

In this case, as per the aforesaid Gazette notification, the market value is fixed at Rs.26,910/- per Square Meter and accordingly the LAO determined the market value and added other statutory benefits.
Undisputedly the said amount has been accepted by the LAO and the compensation was decided on the basis of the said guidance value published in Gazette notification.

When the LAO considered the said market value certainly the Arbitrator ought to have considered the said fact and the Arbitrator in the judgment have not given any special reason that why guidance value published in the Gazette notification on 01.01.2019 is not applicable to the facts of this case and how the market value determined in the subsequent sale deed can be accepted A.P. No.10/2025 as the market value to the acquired property is not at all explained in the judgment.
.18.

It is also not the grievance of the respondent No.1 in the application for enhancement of compensation that the respondent No.3 / LAO has not granted the compensation as contemplated under the aforesaid provisions of Right to Fair Compensation and Transparency in Land Acquisition, Rehabilitation and Resettlement Act, 2013.

entities.text: Right to Fair Compensation and Transparency in Land Acquisition, Rehabilitation and Resettlement Act, 2013
entities.label: STATUTE

sentences.text: There is no material on record to show that the LAO has not calculated the interest as per guidelines given in the aforesaid provision of law to determine the market value.
Under such circumstances, certainly the award passed by the LAO cannot be accepted.

.19. It is also not the case of the petitioner before the LAO or Arbitrator that the respondent No.3 /
LAO has not awarded the compensation as stated in the aforesaid provision of law.

The award /
judgment passed by the Arbitrator / respondent No.2 also nowhere discloses that the LAO has not considered the A.P. No.10/2025 parameter of the aforesaid provision of law i.e., Sections 26 to 30 of Right to Fair Compensation and Transparency in Land Acquisition, Rehabilitation and Resettlement Act, 2013 to determine the market value.

entities.text: Right to Fair Compensation and Transparency in Land Acquisition, Rehabilitation and Resettlement Act, 2013
entities.label: STATUTE

sentences.text: The Gazette notification produced by the petitioner sufficiently discloses that the respondent No.3/ LAO considered the guidance value for registration of sale deeds or agreements to sell and awarded the said amount as compensation.

When the LAO has granted the compensation as per Section 26(1)(a) of Right to Fair Compensation and Transparency in Land Acquisition, Rehabilitation and Resettlement Act, 2013, certainly the Arbitrator is estopped from enhancing the compensation.

entities.text: Right to Fair Compensation and Transparency in Land Acquisition, Rehabilitation and Resettlement Act, 2013
entities.label: STATUTE

sentences.text: The Arbitrator in the aforesaid judgment nowhere stated or discussed or pointed out that the Arbitrator has not followed the aforesaid provisions of law in determining the market value.
It is also not the case of the respondent No.1 before the respondent No.2 that the LAO has not passed the individual award.
Therefore, it is clear that the respondent No.3 / LAO A.P. No.10/2025 has passed individual award by considering all the relevant facts.
Under such circumstances, certainly the award passed by the LAO cannot be set aside or modified or changed.
In view of all these facts, certainly the award passed by the Arbitrator cannot be accepted and that should be intervened by the Court.
Hence, this Court is of the humble opinion that the petitioner has made out sufficient grounds to intervene with the award passed by the Arbitrator and the award is liable to be set aside.
Accordingly, the above point is held in the affirmative.

The respondent No.1 being not satisfied with the said award passed by the LAO / respondent No.3, filed an application before the respondent No.2 / Arbitrator and Special Deputy Commissioner seeking enhancement of compensation.
opennyai_summary.arguments: The Arbitral Award is contrary to the principles of natural justice and shocks the conscience of the Court and the impugned award amount is opposed to most basic notions of morality and justice and thus opposed to fundamental policy of Indian law and deserves to be set aside under Section 34(2)(b)(ii) of the Arbitration and Conciliation Act.
opennyai_summary.issue:
"Whether the impugned award of the Arbitrator/SLAO is against law, fact, evidence and probabilities of the case and liable to be intervened by this Court?"
.8.
opennyai_summary.ANALYSIS:
In the aforesaid facts whenever there is an application for enhancement of compensation before the Arbitrator is filed then it is the duty of the Arbitrator to see that whether the LAO followed Sections 26 to 30 of A.P. No.10/2025 the New Act along with first schedule to the Act.
There is no material on record to show that the LAO has not calculated the interest as per guidelines given in the aforesaid provision of law to determine the market value.
The award /
judgment passed by the Arbitrator / respondent No.2 also nowhere discloses that the LAO has not considered the A.P. No.10/2025 parameter of the aforesaid provision of law i.e., Sections 26 to 30 of Right to Fair Compensation and Transparency in Land Acquisition, Rehabilitation and Resettlement Act, 2013 to determine the market value.
The Gazette notification produced by the petitioner sufficiently discloses that the respondent No.3/ LAO considered the guidance value for registration of sale deeds or agreements to sell and awarded the said amount as compensation.
When the LAO has granted the compensation as per Section 26(1)(a) of Right to Fair Compensation and Transparency in Land Acquisition, Rehabilitation and Resettlement Act, 2013, certainly the Arbitrator is estopped from enhancing the compensation.
The Arbitrator in the aforesaid judgment nowhere stated or discussed or pointed out that the Arbitrator has not followed the aforesaid provisions of law in determining the market value.
It is also not the case of the respondent No.1 before the respondent No.2 that the LAO has not passed the individual award.
Therefore, it is clear that the respondent No.3 / LAO A.P. No.10/2025 has passed individual award by considering all the relevant facts.
Under such circumstances, certainly the award passed by the LAO cannot be set aside or modified or changed.
opennyai_summary.decision:
Accordingly, the above point is held in the affirmative.
In the result following:
National Highways Authority Of India vs Sujith Vijayraghavan on 3 February, 2026 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/123075162/
8 ORDER Petition filed under Section 34(2) of the Arbitration and Conciliation Act,
1996 by the petitioner is hereby allowed.
Consequently, the award passed by the Arbitrator / respondent No.2 in case No. LAQ / ARB / NH-844 / CR / 242/ 2022-23 dated 03.10.2024 pertaining to Sy. No.13/1 (Site No.241) measuring 111.48 Sq. Meters Sq. feet of Marasuru village is hereby set aside with a A.P. No.10/2025 liberty to the parties to pursue their remedy in accordance with law.
Office is directed to send back the Lower Court Records.
